tagline: Out of the Piedmont farms and over the South Mountains.
intro: NC 226 starts among the farms north of Shelby and runs 34 miles to Marion, leaving the rolling Piedmont for the mountains. Corn fields and apple orchards keep it company. At Polkville, in the First Broad River valley, the South Mountains come into view ahead, and the road goes over them.
Off to the southwest stands Cherry Mountain. It got its name from the cherry bounce brewed out of local cherries after the Civil War.

moments.title: Polkville
moments.text: A small Cleveland County town where three state highways meet, and where NC 226 sets off northwest over the South Mountains to Marion.

moments.title: South Mountains State Park
moments.text: In a deeply eroded range the Cherokee once called the Oakanoahs, High Shoals Falls drops more than 80 feet down a sheer cliff into a deep pool.

moments.title: Marion
moments.text: Main Street was mostly wood until a Sunday morning fire in November 1894 burned it nearly to the ground, and the rebuilt downtown is now on the National Register.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, South Mountain Scenery
